This game started as a joke. Now my joke has 1,010 hours logged and I’m divorced. She took the kids. She took the dog. She took the house. She even took the car, which was technically in my name, but apparently that doesn’t matter when you’re the guy who spent every night staring at a virtual bakery instead of “being present.” I tried to explain golden cookie RNG to the judge. He didn’t care. Nobody cared. Everything I loved was stripped from me in the settlement, except for Cookie Clicker. And that’s the problem.

Every time I thought I was done, a golden cookie spawned and whispered “one more.” Suddenly I’m calculating optimal Pantheon setups like it’s a second job that doesn’t pay me. I can name every plant in the garden but I can’t remember my mom’s birthday.

At some point I stopped clicking the cookie. The cookie started clicking me.

11/10. Would sacrifice family stability for +5% CpS again.

I've been playing ever since it was just a browser game. This is THE idle clicker game in my mind. It's the first one I can really remember blowing up in my life. If you want a good way to waste a few hours, this is the game for you.

You click the cookie. Clicking the cookie facilitates buying buildings that help getting more cookies. Eventually you get upgrades to make those buildings more efficient. Eventually you get a sugar lump that unlocks minigames that also increase cookie productivity. Eventually you call upon magic, the stock market, the art of gardening, and gods to get more cookies. Eventually you research something that makes your unpaid elderly workforce more productive, then begin a series of events that leads to touching powers beyond our comprehension, drowning the world in a deluge of baked goods and chocolate, all in the pursuit of getting more cookies.

The world ends as eldritch abominations walk the earth, personally invited by you on the promise of more cookies. With the world in ruins, you discover you are no longer productive enough to acquire the next tier of upgrades in a reasonable amount of time. You use the giant cookie as the catalyst to bring about your own end, ridding yourself of your mortal shell, and the screen goes dark - but this is not game over. In death your are only given more power to get more cookies at impossible rates. You are brought back to a familiar screen - one giant cookie to click on, a blank middle column, and rows of buildings and upgrades to choose from.

You click the cookie.

This is one of those incremental games, where you buy stuff to get currency to buy more stuff. Kind of like Armory and Machine or any number of others.

What makes this special is that it is an exemplary example of the genre. The scaling mechanics are smooth and meaningful, a lot of thought was put into the numbers and making them work. It also has fun minigames and mechanics that you play actively rather than just idling between purchasing sprees. The combos in both active and passive play can get very involved and are quite fun to set up and exploit, and as the growth rate levels out you have more and more incentive to do so.

Lastly the game has a unique feel to it, and a surrealist sense of humor. You start off just baking cookies and hiring grandmothers to cook more but it quickly get very weird both with no explanation and while making perfect sense. I don't want to spoil anything but... ya you can trigger a lot of weird events that turn the whole dynamic of how you play on its head depending on what style you are going for.

Anyway its a good game, it is an idle incremental game, it is one of the best of its type, it has surrealist humor. If that sounds like your thing you will probably love it.

I love cookies, I hate the fact that I stuck through with playing this game until I completed it in its entirety. My laptop is now broken from the sheer amount of hours and months I left it continuously running in order to click cookies, hours which don't even properly show on steam. Not even kidding, I left it running on my screen for so long that even when exiting the game you can see the game still because it burned onto my screen. I'm thankful to finally be finished, I might not be able to even look at a cookie for the next few months, let alone eat one.

All in all, good game, it was a humorous challenge working to get all the achievements. I'm sure my steam friends (who were frequently commenting over the fact I was playing this constantly at one point) are going to be happy to see the notification of me playing this no longer appear, and for me to finally be offline. This game was quite the challenge to complete, and finally being finished I truly feel accomplished. Would I recommend it to my friends? Maybe to the ones who I want to suffer.

I am sure you will be tempted to buy this game thanks to the "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews. Please read this before you do as it will save you heartache, a refund, or worse.

This is not an "immediate satisfaction" style game, as I sadly found out. You have to idle this game for weeks before things start to get interesting.

Yes, weeks.

If that is your cup of tea, grab it. It is NOT my cup of tea, and hence the negative review. A good idle game balances online and offline components. This game does not. I am nearly 80 hours in and I'm nowhere near close to ascending even once. The recommended ascension (according to Reddit, the wiki, and third parties) is between 200 and 440, I'm at...3. At this rate, it will take me a month or two before I ascend.

EDIT: One of the top reviews mentioned using mods in order to speed this game along/make it fun. If you have to do that, the game has poor design. Why?!

Don't get me wrong, the gameplay itself is fun, but it is too slow.

As you descend into madness you are reminded of one thing... cookies. You've worked so hard, waited hours, broke your mouse, installed an autoclicker. Now it is finally time to get this new upgrade. You click the button... silence. Your CPS increases slightly... You feel... nothing. The absence of emotion swiftly changes to confusion. Did I do all that, for nothing? Before you can answer that question you set your eyes on the next purchese. All you can think of is one thing... cookies.

I played this game for what felt like an hour but when I closed it I realized it had been 2 months, my friends no longer talk to me because of my "addiction", and my family is begging me to get help. i don't know what to do... i guess i'll just play some more cookie clicker...

10/10 would recommend
